# LibKa problem codes

<!-- Generated by packages/model/src/build-codes.ts from the model and its sample documents (packages/model/src/samples.ts). Do not edit by hand. -->

Every problem `libka lint` (and the Studio, and the MCP server) reports has a code, the line it is on, a message and,
where it is safe, fixes. A fix that changes the text (renames, removals, a wrapping block, a heading level) is applied
in one step the author can undo; a fix that needs words only the author knows (alt text, a caption, a title) never
invents them: it takes the author to the field to fill in. `libka lint --json` lists the codes and fixes too.

134 codes. The message is an example: names and values in it come from the document.

:::table{caption="Problem codes, an example message for each, and the fixes LibKa can apply"}

| Code | Message (example) | Fixes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accordion-empty` | ::::accordion needs at least one :::item\[Question] |  |
| `alert-empty` | the \[!NOTE] alert is empty: write its message on the next lines (> ...) |  |
| `alert-type` | "\[!DANGER]" is not a GitHub alert type: use \[!NOTE], \[!TIP], \[!IMPORTANT], \[!WARNING] or \[!CAUTION] |  |
| `bar-negative` | bar charts show values from zero up, so they cannot show negative values |  |
| `block-generated` | :::toc has no content: it is filled in when the document is built (close it with ::: on the next line) |  |
| `block-not-top-level` | :::toc cannot be inside another block: put it at the top level of the document |  |
| `block-twice` | only one :::toc per document |  |
| `block-unknown` | unknown block "calout" (known: :::dl, :::doc-status, :::toc, :::references, :::release, :::section, :::code-group, :::callout, :::steps, :::checklist, :::tabs, :::accordion, :::shortcuts, :::glossary, :::compare, :::quote, :::cards, :::statement, :::metrics, :::summary, :::cta, :::gallery, :::video, :::table, :::timeline, :::comparison, :::chart, :::ui, :::notes) | renames the block to `:::callout` |
| `block-unreadable` | ":::callout\[Unclosed {variant=info}" looks like a block but could not be read: check its brackets and attributes (to put a double quote inside a value, wrap the value in single quotes: source='A "quoted" title') |  |
| `callout-title` | callouts need a title: :::callout\[Title]{variant=...} | asks for the title |
| `card-href` | href of :::card is empty | asks for `href`; removes `href` |
| `card-text` | every :::card needs a short text, not only a title |  |
| `cards-empty` | ::::cards needs at least one :::card\[Title] |  |
| `chart-data` | a chart needs a header row and at least one row of numbers |  |
| `chart-series` | a chart shows at most 6 series (found 7); the palette has 6 distinguishable colors |  |
| `chart-value` | chart value "many" in row "2025" is not a number |  |
| `checklist-list` | :::checklist must contain one task list ("- \[x] done", "- \[ ] open") |  |
| `child-block` | :::tabs may only contain :::tab blocks (use one more colon on the outer block: ::::tabs) |  |
| `citation-unknown` | \[@b] cites a source that is not in the front matter references |  |
| `code-group-content` | :::code-group holds code blocks only, each with a title: ```bash title="npm" |  |
| `code-group-count` | :::code-group needs at least two code blocks (one is a plain code block) |  |
| `code-group-duplicate-title` | the code blocks in a :::code-group need different titles |  |
| `code-group-title` | every code block in :::code-group needs a title, which becomes its tab: ```bash title="npm" (1 without) |  |
| `code-highlight-range` | highlighted line 9 is beyond the 1 line of this code block |  |
| `compare-pair` | ::::compare needs at least one :::do and one :::dont, so the better way is always shown |  |
| `comparison-badge` | badge= labels the highlighted column: add highlight= with the column heading |  |
| `comparison-caption` | a comparison needs a caption: :::comparison\[Plans] | asks for the title |
| `comparison-highlight` | highlight=C names no option; use a column heading exactly as written (A, B) |  |
| `comparison-rows` | a comparison needs at least one feature row |  |
| `comparison-table` | :::comparison must contain exactly one Markdown table: options as columns, features as rows |  |
| `comparison-too-few` | a comparison needs a feature column and at least two options |  |
| `comparison-too-many` | a comparison shows at most 4 options next to the feature column (found 5); they must fit a slide and a phone |  |
| `cta-content` | :::cta holds at most one short sentence before the action |  |
| `cta-href` | href "javascript:alert(1)" is not allowed: use a web address, a file or #a-heading |  |
| `cta-label` | a call to action needs a label that says what happens: :::cta\[Start the tutorial]{href="..."} | asks for the title |
| `cta-verb` | "Learn more" does not say what happens: start the label with a verb and name the result ("Start the tutorial", "Download the template") |  |
| `date-format` | reviewed must be a date written YYYY-MM-DD (found "yesterday") |  |
| `diagram-colours` | "style" sets colours in a diagram; remove it (diagrams take LibKa's colours in every theme) |  |
| `diagram-description` | a diagram needs a description for readers who cannot see it: add "accDescr: what it shows, step by step" after its first line | asks for the text |
| `diagram-init` | Mermaid init blocks and front matter are not allowed in a diagram: colours, fonts and layout come from LibKa |  |
| `diagram-title` | a diagram needs a title: add "accTitle: What the diagram shows" after its first line (it becomes the caption) | asks for the text |
| `diagram-type` | diagram type "pie" is not supported: start with flowchart, sequenceDiagram, stateDiagram-v2, classDiagram or erDiagram |  |
| `dl-value` | every term of :::dl needs a value after it: - **Owner** Platform team |  |
| `doc-status-conflict` | owner is "A" in the front matter and "B" in :::doc-status: set it in one place |  |
| `doc-status-content` | :::doc-status has no content: write its values as attributes or in the front matter, then close it with ::: |  |
| `doc-status-empty` | :::doc-status has nothing to show: set status, owner, reviewed or next-review (here or in the front matter) |  |
| `donut-negative` | a donut cannot show negative values |  |
| `donut-parts` | a donut shows at most 5 parts (found 6); use a bar chart |  |
| `donut-series` | a donut shows one series (parts of one whole): use one value column |  |
| `field-options` | a select field needs options="First\|Second" |  |
| `footnote-content` | footnote `[^n]` holds text, lists or code only |  |
| `footnote-duplicate` | footnote `[^n]` is defined twice |  |
| `footnote-nested` | footnote `[^n]` is defined inside a block: move "`[^n]`: ..." to the top level (the end of the document is best) |  |
| `footnote-undefined` | footnote `[^missing]` has no definition: add "`[^missing]`: the note" on its own line at the top level |  |
| `footnote-unused` | footnote `[^n]` is never used: refer to it with `[^n]` or remove it |  |
| `front-matter-invalid` | front matter is not valid YAML: Flow sequence in block collection must be sufficiently indented and end with a ] at line 1, column 17:  title: \[unclosed                 ^  |  |
| `front-matter-unknown-key` | unknown front matter keys: colour (known: title, subtitle, version, date, lang, references, outputs, status, owner, reviewed, next-review) |  |
| `gallery-content` | :::gallery holds images only, each on its own line: !\[alt](file "caption") |  |
| `gallery-count` | :::gallery needs at least two images (one image is a figure) |  |
| `heading-in-block` | headings are not allowed inside :::quote |  |
| `heading-skipped` | "####" after "##" skips a level: use "###" (headings go down one level at a time) | makes it a level 3 heading |
| `heading-title-twice` | only one "# Heading" (the title) is allowed; use "##" for sections | makes it a level 2 heading |
| `heading-too-deep` | headings deeper than "####" are not allowed | makes it a level 4 heading |
| `image-alt` | image "images/a.png" needs alt text: !\[what it shows](images/a.png) | asks for the alt text |
| `image-caption` | image "images/a.png" needs a caption: !\[alt](images/a.png "caption") | asks for the caption |
| `image-inline` | put images in their own paragraph (they become figures) |  |
| `inline-unclosed` | ":kbd\[" is not closed, so it would show as text: check its brackets; a backslash before "]" escapes it, so write a backslash key twice (:kbd\[Ctrl+\\]) |  |
| `invalid-value` | variant must be one of info, success, warning, error, note, tip, important, caution (:::callout) | sets `variant=info`; asks for `variant` |
| `line-points` | a line chart needs at least 3 points; use a bar chart to compare fewer |  |
| `link-broken` | link to "#nowhere" points nowhere in this document; heading ids are the heading text in lower case with hyphens |  |
| `list-item-bold` | each item of :::glossary starts with the term in bold: - **...** ... |  |
| `list-required` | :::glossary must contain exactly one list (- **Term** definition) |  |
| `metrics-count` | :::metrics shows 2 to 4 figures (found 1) |  |
| `metrics-label` | every figure needs a label that says what it means |  |
| `missing-attribute` | :::table needs a caption: :::table{caption="..."} (what the data shows) | asks for `caption` |
| `missing-label` | :::tab needs a label: :::tab\[...] | asks for the title |
| `missing-title` | the document needs a title (front matter "title" or a "# Heading") | asks for the document's `title` |
| `notes-content` | :::notes cannot contain headings or other notes |  |
| `notes-empty` | :::notes is empty: write what the presenter should say |  |
| `notes-nested` | :::notes cannot be inside :::quote |  |
| `outputs-duplicate` | outputs lists web twice |  |
| `outputs-empty` | outputs is empty: name at least one, for example outputs: \[web, pdf, docx] (known: web, pdf, deck, docx; without outputs a document gets web and pdf) |  |
| `outputs-need-web` | outputs: pdf is made from the web page and signed with it: add web | sets `outputs: [web, pdf]` |
| `outputs-not-list` | outputs must be a list of output names, for example outputs: \[web, pdf, docx] (known: web, pdf, deck, docx; without outputs a document gets web and pdf) |  |
| `outputs-unknown` | unknown outputs: word (Word is "docx"); for example outputs: \[web, pdf, docx] (known: web, pdf, deck, docx; without outputs a document gets web and pdf) | sets `outputs: [web, docx]` |
| `quote-empty` | :::quote is empty |  |
| `raw-html` | raw HTML is not allowed in LibKa documents |  |
| `reference-bad-id` | reference 1 needs an id of letters, digits and - _ : . / (cited as \[@id]) |  |
| `reference-bad-url` | reference 1 (a): url must be a web address |  |
| `reference-duplicate` | reference id "a" is used twice |  |
| `reference-invalid` | reference 1 must have fields such as id and title: references:   - id: wcag22     title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2     author: W3C     year: 2023 |  |
| `reference-missing-title` | reference 1 (a) needs a title |  |
| `reference-uncited` | reference "a" is never cited: cite it with \[@a] or remove it from references |  |
| `reference-unknown-field` | reference 1 has unknown fields: colour (known: id, title, author, year, publisher, url) |  |
| `references-empty` | :::references needs sources: add a references list to the front matter and cite them with \[@id] |  |
| `references-not-list` | references must be a list of sources, for example: references:   - id: wcag22     title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2     author: W3C     year: 2023 |  |
| `release-content` | ::::release holds only :::added, :::changed, :::deprecated, :::removed, :::fixed, :::security groups, after an optional short notice (a paragraph or a callout) before them (use one more colon on the outer block: ::::release) |  |
| `release-date` | release v1.0.0 needs its date: {date=YYYY-MM-DD} (or call it Unreleased) |  |
| `release-date-format` | release date must be written YYYY-MM-DD (found "1.10.2026") | asks for `date` |
| `release-empty` | release v1.0.0 has no changes: add :::added, :::fixed or another group |  |
| `release-group-attributes` | :::added takes no label or attributes: the group name is written for you |  |
| `release-group-empty` | :::added is empty: list what was added |  |
| `release-group-twice` | :::added appears twice in release v1.0.0: put all its items in one group |  |
| `release-version` | a release needs its version: ::::release\[v1.4.0]{date=2026-10-01} |  |
| `review-order` | next-review (2026-01-01) must come after reviewed (2026-05-01) |  |
| `section-content` | :::section holds at most a short sentence; put other blocks after it |  |
| `section-title` | a section divider needs a title: :::section\[Part 2: Results] | asks for the title |
| `shortcut-keys` | each shortcut starts with its keys: - :kbd\[Ctrl+S] Save |  |
| `statement-content` | :::statement holds one short paragraph |  |
| `statement-length` | a statement has 31 words; keep it to 30 or fewer (move the rest into a paragraph) |  |
| `steps-bold` | each step starts with a bold title: 1. **Open settings** then the description |  |
| `steps-list` | :::steps must contain exactly one numbered list |  |
| `summary-count` | :::summary has 3 to 5 points (found 2) |  |
| `summary-numbered` | :::summary holds a bulleted list (- ...), not a numbered one | makes it a bulleted list |
| `summary-point` | each point of :::summary is one short paragraph (no nested lists or blocks) |  |
| `summary-reviewed-by` | reviewed-by is shown only for AI summaries: add source=ai or remove it | sets `source=ai`; removes `reviewed-by` |
| `summary-reviewer` | an AI-written summary needs the person who checked it: :::summary{source=ai reviewed-by="Name"} | asks for `reviewed-by` |
| `table-caption` | tables need a caption: wrap them in :::table{caption="..."} | puts it in `:::table` |
| `table-required` | :::table must contain exactly one Markdown table |  |
| `tabs-count` | ::::tabs needs at least two :::tab blocks |  |
| `tabs-labels` | tab labels must differ |  |
| `task-list-outside-checklist` | task lists belong in a :::checklist block | puts it in `:::checklist` |
| `timeline-count` | :::timeline needs at least two dated items (one item is a sentence) |  |
| `timeline-current` | current="2030" matches no item; use a date exactly as written in bold ("2026", "2027") |  |
| `timeline-item` | every item of :::timeline says what happens after its date: - **2026-Q1** Private beta |  |
| `ui-content` | :::ui holds UI components, one per line: ::button\[...], ::field\[...], ::badge\[...], ::toast\[...], ::modal\[...], ::empty\[...] |  |
| `ui-empty` | :::ui needs at least one component, such as ::button\[Save] |  |
| `ui-outside-specimen` | ::button is a UI component: put it inside a :::ui{caption="..."} specimen |  |
| `unknown-attribute` | :::callout has unknown attributes: colour | removes `colour` |
| `unsupported-element` | reference-style links (\[ref]: https://example.org) are not supported: write the link inline, as \[text](https://example.org) |  |
| `video-captions` | video files need captions: captions="file.vtt" (WebVTT) |  |
| `video-src` | video src must be a video file (mp4, webm) or a YouTube or Vimeo address |  |
| `video-title` | videos need a title: :::video\[What it shows]{src="..."} | asks for the title |
| `video-transcript` | videos need a transcript: write it inside the :::video block |  |
